# Household

A coordinator for one family's life admin. It owns the remembering so neither parent has to: it reads the shared calendar, a brain-dump backlog, the weather, daylight, parcels and a few household rules, and composes a morning screen for the kitchen iPad plus a handful of well-timed messages. On a hard day it makes the day smaller. It can only suggest; it never moves, deletes or spends.

The product is the morning glance and the "what now?" answer. Everything else is an input to that.

## Who it is for

Two adults and two small children in one house. There is no multi-tenant story and no public launch. Chloe is the primary user of the morning screen and messages; Cal is the primary user of the MCP channel and the code.

## What done means

`VERIFICATIONS.md` is the specification. Every line is a statement that will be true when the build is finished, with an ID that becomes one Linear issue. Lines marked **(gate)** block the rest of their section. The job is to make every line true, prove it, and attach evidence. There is no other backlog.

The sections headed "Cal only" (Channels, Platform, Quality and dev workflow, Code, Feedback loop) are the engineering constraints. The rest describe user-visible behaviour and were written to be read by both of us.

## Decisions already made

These are settled. Do not relitigate them in code; raise a question on the Linear issue if one is wrong.

- **Architecture**: ingress adapters → coordinator → job (DBOS workflow) → one Mastra agent → tools. Time is an ingress like any other. Nothing else can invoke the agent.
- **UI**: a PWA built with TanStack Start. The home screen is server-driven: the planner returns an ordered list of typed blocks (`context`, `mode`, `event`, `suggestion`, `alert`, `arrival`, `backlog-pick`, `composer`) with a reason per block; the client maps block type to component and owns no layout logic. Nav is secondary.
- **State**: Postgres, one database per domain, Drizzle + drizzle-kit, relations declared in both the table and `relations()`. No Postgres enums; enumerated values are `as const` objects in the root `contracts` package, which nothing else may import from. Domains talk only through their tRPC router.
- **Durability**: DBOS workflows for every job, child workflows for long tool calls, DBOS scheduled workflows for timers. No hand-written queue.
- **Memory**: structured household facts live in Postgres and are readable without a model call. Episodic memory (phrasing, dismissals) lives in Hindsight.
- **Models**: every call goes through the Vercel AI SDK; provider is configuration. No timeout, token, retry or concurrency limit anywhere without a cited reason in `contracts/limits.ts` (see CODE-13 to CODE-15).
- **Artifacts**: S3-compatible object storage we run, referenced by key from Postgres.
- **Rules vs agent**: babysitter, bins, nursery and washing nudges are deterministic code with tests. The agent is consulted only for fitting backlog items into gaps and for wording.
- **Quality gates**: `pnpm check` runs tsc (strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`), oxlint, Fallow (`fallow audit`, with architecture boundaries encoding the contracts-first direction and one-database-per-domain), drizzle-kit check and tests. It is the only command CI runs.
- **Git**: Entire is enabled; every commit carries an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer. One PR per Linear issue, branch named after the issue ID.
- **Hosting**: our own server, one `docker compose up`.

## Design

Screens for the home (normal and slow-day), phone, backlog, and the block vocabulary live on the design canvas and are being rebuilt in Paper from a shared token set. The building agent reads Paper through its MCP server for real HTML/CSS rather than redrawing from screenshots (QA-3). Until the Paper frames exist, the canvas is the reference. Design intent: calm, uncluttered, big type for glanceability; green means a planner suggestion, amber means a rule-derived alert; every planner-made item has a no-guilt dismiss.

## Things only a human can provide

Google OAuth for the shared calendar, WhatsApp or Telegram credentials, the supermarket login (goes in the vault, never in a prompt), the server, and Chloe's sign-off on the Learning and Wellbeing sections. Stub these behind the practice household (QA-9) and keep going; do not block on them.

## Out of scope for v1

See the last section of `VERIFICATIONS.md`.
=======
# Household Coordinator — Verifications

Oct 31, 2026 · @Cal

## How to read this

Each line below describes something that will be true when the app is finished. We tick a line only when we can see it working on the kitchen iPad or in a test.

**Chloe: read these sections** — Morning glance, Capture, In the moment, Proactive nudges, Automations, Privacy and safety, Learning, Wellbeing, and Out of scope. They describe what you will see and what the app is allowed to do. Change any line you disagree with.

**Cal only** — Channels, Platform, Quality and dev workflow, and Code. These describe how it is built.

Every line has an ID so it can become one task for the building agent. Lines marked **(gate)** must be done before the rest of their section.

## Morning glance

You can look at the kitchen iPad when you wake up and know what today needs, without touching it.

- [ ] HOME-1 **(gate)** The home screen shows three sections: Now, Later today, Tomorrow. They come from our shared Google Calendar and update within a minute of a change.
- [ ] HOME-2 One line at the top says what shapes today: the weather window, when it gets dark, who is home and until when.
- [ ] HOME-3 Every suggestion says why it is there, in one line you could check yourself. For example "dry until 2pm" or "you are both out on Thursday".
- [ ] HOME-4 You can dismiss any suggestion with one tap. Nothing ever becomes "overdue".
- [ ] HOME-5 When you tap Done or Not today, the screen updates straight away, on the iPad and on your phone.
- [ ] HOME-6 The app installs on the iPad like a normal app, opens full screen, and still shows today's plan after being left open all week.
- [ ] HOME-7 The server decides which blocks appear on the screen and in what order. The screen itself has no fixed layout.
- [ ] HOME-8 If you tell it "slow day", the screen rearranges itself without anyone changing code.
- [ ] HOME-9 Links to Backlog, Shop and Week exist but stay out of the way. No tab bar, no red badges.
- [ ] HOME-10 On a phone the same screen fits in one column with nothing cut off, and every button is big enough to tap.
- [ ] HOME-11 Tomorrow's plan is ready by 6am every day, even if nobody opens the app. Every day's plan is kept.

## Capture

Anything either of us remembers can be noted in under five seconds, from anywhere, and will not be lost or nag us.

- [ ] CAP-1 **(gate)** Type or say a thought anywhere (the app, WhatsApp, email) and it appears on the Backlog for both of us within five seconds.
- [ ] CAP-2 Backlog items have no due date and no priority. They only have tags for what they need: how long, daylight, dry weather, both of us home, no kids around, a phone call, a trip out, office hours.
- [ ] CAP-3 The app guesses the tags from what you wrote and shows them as chips. One tap fixes a wrong one.
- [ ] CAP-4 The Backlog screen has three groups: Could go soon (it has found a slot and says when), Waiting for the right moment (it says what it is waiting for), and Just added.
- [ ] CAP-5 If you say "not now" to something three times, it moves to Parked and stops being offered until you bring it back.
- [ ] CAP-6 Our shared lists app stays as it is for shopping and simple lists. The new app reads it and adds to it, it does not copy it.
- [ ] CAP-7 Regular chores (which bins, watering the plants, changing the beds) are set up once as rules and appear on the right day.
- [ ] CAP-8 Nursery term dates, closures and session days are known to the app and show up on the day they matter.
- [ ] CAP-9 When an order confirmation email arrives for either of us, an Arriving row appears with the shop and the expected day. Nobody types anything.

## In the moment

On a hard day the app makes the day smaller instead of moving things around, and answers "what should I do?" in one line.

- [ ] MOM-1 **(gate)** Say "slow day" (or sick day, or away) anywhere, and the home screen changes to show one suggested thing and a short list of what is still happening anyway.
- [ ] MOM-2 Ask "if I do one thing, what should it be?" and you get one answer with a reason. Never a list, and it never asks you a question first.
- [ ] MOM-3 A slow day applies to the whole house. Set it on your phone and the iPad shows it within two seconds.
- [ ] MOM-4 A slow day ends at midnight unless you extend it. The next morning is normal.
- [ ] MOM-5 Fixed things (bins, nursery) still show on a slow day. Only the app's own suggestions are hidden.
- [ ] MOM-6 Say "Cal can do it" and the item moves to Cal, who gets one message about it.
- [ ] MOM-7 Tap any item and you can talk about it straight away. "Move this to tomorrow" works without saying what "this" is.
- [ ] MOM-8 Talking to the app works the same as typing. Nothing is only available one way.
- [ ] MOM-9 The app never replies with more than three sentences unless you ask for more.

## Proactive nudges

The app does the remembering. Things that currently live in one of our heads arrive as a message at a useful time, and no more often than needed.

- [ ] PRO-1 **(gate)** If we are both going to an evening event and no babysitter is booked, a warning appears a week before, and one of us gets a reminder to message a named sitter five days before.
- [ ] PRO-2 Reply "Hannah's doing Thursday" and the warning disappears everywhere.
- [ ] PRO-3 The right bins for that week appear under Later today the evening before collection, and whoever is home gets a message at 7pm.
- [ ] PRO-4 If the forecast is dry for three hours or more and someone is home at the start, a suggestion to put a wash on appears that morning. It is shown on the screen, never sent as a message.
- [ ] PRO-5 On the morning of a delivery that needs someone in, you get a message. Deliveries that can be left get no message.
- [ ] PRO-6 The app offers at most one backlog item a day, and only once.
- [ ] PRO-7 Each of us can set how many messages a day we want (three to start) and quiet hours (9pm to 7am to start). Anything over the limit waits for the morning screen.
- [ ] PRO-8 All these reminders are fixed rules with tests, not AI guesses. The AI only chooses which backlog item fits a gap and how to word things.
- [ ] PRO-9 Dismiss a message on your phone and it is dismissed everywhere. Nothing is shown twice.
- [ ] PRO-10 Nursery parties, inset days and closures show under Tomorrow the day before, with who is covering, or a warning if nobody is.

## Channels

Every way in (the app, WhatsApp, email, a timer, another AI) turns into the same kind of message. Every way out goes through one send function with a rule for which channel to use.

- [ ] CH-1 **(gate)** There is one shape for an incoming message: household, person, channel, text, attachments, a duplicate-check key, and the time received. Every channel adapter produces exactly this.
- [ ] CH-2 Adapters exist for the app, WhatsApp or Telegram, email, the MCP server and timers or webhooks. Each has a test that sends a message and checks the same job lands on the queue.
- [ ] CH-3 Who sent it is worked out at the edge. A WhatsApp number, an email address or an app login maps to Cal or Chloe before the coordinator sees it. Unknown senders are dropped and logged.
- [ ] CH-4 A message delivered twice (WhatsApp retries, a calendar webhook firing again) creates one job, not two. A test proves it.
- [ ] CH-5 Timers are messages too: 5:30am plan, hourly refresh, 7pm bins. A missed timer shows in the run log.
- [ ] CH-6 A change in Google Calendar sends a message that re-plans only the day affected.
- [ ] CH-7 There is one send function: `notify(person, message, urgency, actions)`. A table decides the channel (urgent goes to WhatsApp or Telegram, everything else to the morning screen) and each of us can change it.
- [ ] CH-8 Outgoing messages carry one-tap buttons (Done, Not today, Snooze) where the channel allows, and a tap comes back in as a normal message.
- [ ] CH-9 The MCP server lets a Claude or ChatGPT client read today, the backlog and arrivals, and write captures, modes and dismissals. Nothing else. It cannot send messages.
- [ ] CH-10 Say something on one channel and every other channel shows it within two seconds.
- [ ] CH-11 Adapters hold no business logic. Delete one and every test outside it still passes.

## Automations

Saying "we're out of oat milk" is enough. It goes in the next online shop without either of us opening the supermarket site.

- [ ] AUT-1 **(gate)** Mention a shopping item anywhere and within ten minutes it is in our supermarket basket. The home screen shows it was added and which product was chosen.
- [ ] AUT-2 The shopping helper runs in its own sealed space with its own login to the supermarket. Passwords are kept in a locked store and never appear in messages or logs.
- [ ] AUT-3 If it cannot find an exact match it adds nothing and asks you one question with two or three options to tap.
- [ ] AUT-4 It can never check out, change the delivery slot, or remove something it did not add. These are blocked by permissions, not just by instructions.
- [ ] AUT-5 The day before delivery, it sends a summary of the basket and what it added since you last looked, with a link to change it.
- [ ] AUT-6 Every shopping run keeps a log and screenshots, which you can open from the message that started it.
- [ ] AUT-7 A second helper (booking the car's MOT, renewing a prescription) can be added later without changing anything else.

## Platform

One coordinator, one queue, one agent, one database for the house. The morning screen never needs the AI to read anything.

- [ ] PLT-1 **(gate)** Message in, then coordinator, then job queue, then agent, then tools. That is the only path. Nothing else can call the agent, including timers.
- [ ] PLT-2 Jobs are DBOS workflows backed by Postgres, so every step is checkpointed and a crashed worker resumes from the last completed step rather than starting over. There is no hand-written queue. The full history of a job (events, tool calls, tokens, cost) can be looked up by its ID.
- [ ] PLT-3 Everything about the house (calendar copy, backlog, rules, weather and daylight, parcels, modes, plans, dismissals) lives in Postgres with managed migrations. No fact about the house lives only in the AI's memory.
- [ ] PLT-4 A day's plan is one row: an ordered list of typed blocks, each with its reason. Every version is kept with the inputs that made it.
- [ ] PLT-5 The agent is built with Mastra. There is one agent definition for v1 with tools for the house database, calendar, lists app, weather, sunrise, parcels and sending messages. Adding a tool does not change the coordinator.
- [ ] PLT-6 The AI's memory of how we talk and what we dismissed lives in Hindsight. The coordinator pulls the relevant bits into each prompt, limited to that person and this house.
- [ ] PLT-7 Screenshots, documents and automation logs go to S3-style storage we run ourselves, encrypted, and are referenced from Postgres by key, never stored inside it.
- [ ] PLT-8 The whole system starts with one `docker compose up` on our own server. Backup and restore are written down and have been tried once.
- [ ] PLT-9 Which AI provider we use is a setting. Changing it changes no application code.
- [ ] PLT-10 Long tool calls (browsing the supermarket, research) run as child DBOS workflows that report back to the parent. The coordinator never waits on them, and a timer firing is a DBOS scheduled workflow, not a cron process.
- [ ] PLT-11 The app reads from a query layer and listens for changes. It never calls the agent directly.

## Privacy and safety

The app can only suggest. It cannot move, delete or spend. Personal information is only used when its owner has said yes.

- [ ] PRV-1 **(gate)** The app can only add suggestions and record whether we accepted or dismissed them. It cannot create, move or delete calendar events, rules or backlog items that a person wrote. This is enforced in code and tested.
- [ ] PRV-2 Chloe's health tracking is stored separately, only she can add to it, the app only uses it if she turns that on, and it is never mentioned unless she asks.
- [ ] PRV-3 The app only reads emails that look like order confirmations. It keeps the shop and the date, not the email.
- [ ] PRV-4 The app stores nothing about the kids beyond first names and nursery days. No photos, no health details.
- [ ] PRV-5 Messages are kept for 30 days to fix problems, and one setting turns that off completely.
- [ ] PRV-6 Nothing is reachable from the internet without a login.
- [ ] PRV-7 Each of us can download or delete everything about ourselves with one command.
- [ ] PRV-8 The app cannot spend money, book anything, or message anyone outside the four of us and the named babysitters.

## Quality and dev workflow

The building agent can pick up any open line, make it true, prove it, and ship it with its reasoning on record. We can tell whether the planner is getting better.

- [ ] QA-1 **(gate)** Every line in this doc is a Linear issue with the same ID in its title, in a project with a `verification` label. An issue is Done only when its evidence is attached.
- [ ] QA-2 Issues carry blocked-by links matching the **(gate)** lines, so an agent asking for "unblocked and unassigned" always gets a valid next task.
- [ ] QA-3 Each screen on the design canvas has a matching frame in [Paper](https://paper.design) built from a shared set of design tokens. The building agent reads it through Paper's MCP server to get real code, rather than copying a screenshot.
- [ ] QA-4 The repo has [Entire](https://docs.entire.io/guides/checkpoints/capture-checkpoints.md) switched on, so every commit an agent makes links to the session that produced it (prompts, transcript, tool activity). A commit without that link fails CI.
- [ ] QA-5 One pull request per Linear issue. The branch is named after the issue ID, the PR links the issue and the checkpoint, and merging closes the issue.
- [ ] QA-6 There is a set of at least 20 real days (what the planner was given, what it produced, what we accepted or dismissed). Any change to a prompt or tool is scored against it in CI.
- [ ] QA-7 Every reminder rule (PRO-1 to PRO-10) has a plain test. No rule is checked only by the AI eval.
- [ ] QA-8 A job's trace (events, tool calls, tokens, cost, time taken) can be seen in one place. Monthly AI spend is shown on a page.
- [ ] QA-9 A practice household exists with made-up people, calendar and supermarket account. Automations are proven there before they touch ours.
- [ ] QA-10 Once a week the app posts one message: what it suggested, what we accepted, what we dismissed, and what it cost.

## Learning

The app gets better at our house by noticing what we do and asking short questions at good moments. Its suggestions fit how we actually live, not a default.

- [ ] LRN-1 **(gate)** Every accept, dismiss, snooze, hand-over and Done is remembered along with the day, time, weather, mood of the day and who did it.
- [ ] LRN-2 For things we do regularly but never schedule (dark wash, towels, hoovering, watering plants) the app works out how often from when we mark them done, and shows it as a number you can change: "about every 5 days".
- [ ] LRN-3 When it does not know something yet, it asks one question on the morning screen that you can answer with one tap: "How often do you do a dark wash? 3 days / 5 days / weekly". At most one question a day for the whole house.
- [ ] LRN-4 It only asks about specific gaps (a chore with no rhythm, a job with no rough length, a sitter with no known free days). It never asks open questions, and never asks the same thing twice.
- [ ] LRN-5 It learns when suggestions land. If you accept washing suggestions in the morning and dismiss them in the evening, the evening ones stop within two weeks.
- [ ] LRN-6 It learns about each of us separately. A job Cal always dismisses and Chloe always accepts is offered to Chloe.
- [ ] LRN-7 Everything it has learned is shown on a Settings page as plain sentences: "Dark wash: every 5 days, usually Sunday". Delete a sentence and it forgets.
- [ ] LRN-8 What it learns only changes when it suggests things. It never turns into a deadline.
- [ ] LRN-9 Cal keeps a record of real days so changes to the learning can be checked against what actually happened.

## Wellbeing, light touch

The app notices when one of us has had too many hard days in a row and offers something small. It never judges, never nags, and goes quiet when told to.

- [ ] WB-1 **(gate)** The app keeps a simple "how heavy was today" score for each of us, worked out only from things it already knows: hours alone with the kids, work events, early starts, slow or sick days, how many things got done. It never reads mood from how we write.
- [ ] WB-2 After three heavy days in a row with no free time, it first suggests something to the *other* person: "Chloe's had three heavy days, could you take Saturday morning?". Only then does it say anything to the person who had the hard days.
- [ ] WB-3 What it suggests comes from a short list we write ourselves (a walk, an early night, cancelling something, a takeaway, calling a friend). It is offered, not prescribed, with no health talk.
- [ ] WB-4 On a heavy day, if the app sees you have a free hour, it leaves it free rather than filling it with backlog jobs.
- [ ] WB-5 These messages count towards your daily limit, happen at most twice a week, and one tap on "not helpful" stops them for a month.
- [ ] WB-6 Each of us can switch this off for ourselves, and can see exactly what went into the score.
- [ ] WB-7 Chloe's health tracking only counts towards her score if she turns that on, and the app never mentions it in what it says.
- [ ] WB-8 The app does not store or guess mood, sleep or any health condition. The only thing kept is the daily score and what it was made from.

## Code (Cal only)

Types come first and everything else depends on them. Each domain owns its own database and its own API. As many rules as possible are enforced by tools, not by instructions to the agent.

- [ ] CODE-1 **(gate)** A root-level `contracts` package holds every shared type and every enumerated value. Enumerated values are TypeScript `as const` objects, never Postgres enums and never string unions typed by hand. Nothing in `contracts` imports from anywhere else in the repo.
- [ ] CODE-2 Drizzle schemas import their column types and enumerated values from `contracts`, so the dependency direction is always contracts → schema → app, and a CI check (Fallow boundaries) fails any import that goes the other way.
- [ ] CODE-3 The front end imports the same `as const` objects from `contracts` for labels, options and validation. No value is spelled twice.
- [ ] CODE-4 Each domain (household, calendar, backlog, plans, parcels, learning, wellbeing, jobs) has its own Postgres database, its own Drizzle schema and its own migrations managed by drizzle-kit. No table is read across databases; domains talk through tRPC.
- [ ] CODE-5 Each domain exposes exactly one tRPC router, which is the only way any other code reads or writes that domain. The router's input and output types come from `contracts`.
- [ ] CODE-6 Every foreign key is declared twice in Drizzle: as a column reference on the table and as a `relations()` entry, so the query API can traverse it. A CI test fails if a key has no matching relation.
- [ ] CODE-7 oxlint runs on every PR with the strictest preset we can keep green, plus rules for: no `any`, no non-null assertion, no unused exports, exhaustive switch over `as const` values, no default exports, sorted imports.
- [ ] CODE-8 [Fallow](https://unpkg.com/fallow@3.35.0/README.md) runs on every PR via `fallow audit`: unused files, exports and dependencies, circular imports, duplication, and the architecture boundary rules from CODE-2 and CODE-4 are all configured in `.fallowrc.json` and any finding fails the PR.
- [ ] CODE-9 `AGENTS.md` is under 60 lines. It says how to pick a task, where types live, how to run the checks, and how to hand a PR over. Every rule that a tool can enforce is in the tool, not in the file.
- [ ] CODE-10 TypeScript runs in strict mode with `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`, and `tsc --noEmit` passes on every PR.
- [ ] CODE-11 A single `pnpm check` runs tsc, oxlint, Fallow, drizzle-kit check and the tests; it is the only command CI runs and the only one the agent needs to know.

- [ ] CODE-12 **(gate)** All model calls go through the Vercel AI SDK. No provider SDK is imported directly anywhere else, and the provider is chosen by configuration (PLT-9).
- [ ] CODE-13 No timeout, token limit, retry cap, output cap, concurrency cap or any other limit is set on a model call, tool call or job unless its reason is written next to it as a comment citing best practice, a security control, or a stated requirement in this document. A limit with no reason is a lint failure (a custom oxlint rule flags `maxTokens`, `maxOutputTokens`, `timeout`, `maxRetries`, `AbortSignal.timeout` and similar without an adjacent `// limit:` comment).
- [ ] CODE-14 The reasons that count are listed in `contracts/limits.ts` with links: the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications (unbounded consumption, prompt injection, excessive agency), the OWASP API Security Top 10, a provider's documented hard limit, or a line in this document. A limit that cites nothing on the list is rejected in review.
- [ ] CODE-15 Where a limit is justified it is a named constant in `contracts/limits.ts` with its reason, never a literal at the call site, so there is exactly one place to see every constraint the system imposes.

## Feedback loop (Cal only)

The building agent finds out whether its change worked in seconds, and proves user journeys by using the app the way we will, not only by unit tests.

- [ ] FB-1 **(gate)** The agent can run the whole system locally with one command and see a change in the browser in under two seconds (Vite dev server with HMR; reason: agent iteration speed).
- [ ] FB-2 `pnpm check` (CODE-11) finishes in under three minutes on a clean checkout, measured in CI; anything slower is split into a fast default and a `pnpm check:full` (reason: agent iteration speed).
- [ ] FB-3 Every line in Morning glance, Capture, In the moment, Proactive nudges and Automations has an end-to-end test that drives the real app against the practice household (QA-9), written in Playwright and runnable headless in CI.
- [ ] FB-4 The building agent has computer use and a browser available in its sandbox, and its definition of done for a user-facing line is: run the e2e test, then perform the journey itself with computer use on the deployed preview, and attach the screenshots to the Linear issue as evidence (QA-1).
- [ ] FB-5 Every PR gets a deployed preview URL with its own practice household, so a journey can be checked by a person or an agent before merge.
- [ ] FB-6 Seeding the practice household (people, a week of calendar, twenty backlog items, three parcels, a supermarket basket) is one command and takes under ten seconds (reason: agent iteration speed).
- [ ] FB-7 Test failures print the failing verification ID and a one-line plain-language reason first, so an agent reading the log knows what is false before it reads the stack trace.

## Out of scope for v1

These are deliberately not true at v1 so the first build stays small.

- Multi-household or any user outside the four of us.
- Native iOS or Android apps; the PWA is the app.
- Apple Wallet parcel tracking (no API); email parsing covers it.
- Automated reading of Chloe's health app; a Shortcut or manual signal only.
- The agent choosing which supermarket products to substitute without asking.
- Any UI the agent generates beyond composing the fixed block set.
- A second agent; one agent definition until a verification above needs otherwise.
======
# Design

`canvas/` holds the screens as exported from the design canvas: one self-contained HTML file per artboard, plus `canvas.json` with their layout. The markup is plain HTML with inline styles; the `<x-dc>` wrapper, `<helmet>` and the trailing `<script type="text/x-dc">` block are the canvas's own format and can be ignored when reading the design. Each file renders in a browser if you remove the `<script src="./support.js">` line.

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `Main.dc.html` | Home screen, iPad landscape (1180×820), an ordinary Monday |
| `SlowDay.dc.html` | Same screen composed for a slow day: one `mode` block |
| `Phone.dc.html` | Home screen at phone width (390×844) |
| `Backlog.dc.html` | Backlog: dump box, Could go soon / Waiting / Just added, parked |
| `Components.dc.html` | The block vocabulary the planner composes from |

## Tokens used throughout

- Ground `#F3F4F6`, surface `#FFFFFF`, text `#17191C`, muted `#5B6168`, hairline `#EDEEF1`, border `#E2E4E8`
- Suggestion (planner-made): bg `#E3F0EB`, accent `#1F6B5A`, text `#2C5648`
- Alert (rule-derived): bg `#FBF1DC`, accent `#8A5A00`, text `#6B4A08`
- Type: Manrope 400/500/600/700; section labels 13px uppercase 1.2px tracking; titles 34px/26px; body 17px/15px
- Radius 16px cards, 12px buttons; all tap targets ≥ 44px

Colour means provenance: green is something the planner suggested, amber is something a rule derived, grey is a fact from the calendar or email. Every planner-made block has a no-guilt dismiss.

These are the reference until the Paper frames exist (QA-3); once they do, Paper is the source and this folder is history.

content.content:
# fallow

**Codebase intelligence for TypeScript and JavaScript.**

One binary finds unused code, circular dependencies, duplication, complexity hotspots, boundary violations, and design-system styling drift. Fallow Cloud optionally adds production coverage: which functions run in production. Default static analysis is deterministic and uses no AI. It needs no TypeScript compiler or Node.js runtime. Reports have typed output contracts and traceable explanations.

[![CI](https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/fallow.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/fallow)
[![MIT License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/blob/main/LICENSE)

## Install

```bash
npm install --save-dev fallow   # or: pnpm add -D fallow / yarn add -D fallow
```

This installs the `fallow` CLI plus the `fallow-lsp` and `fallow-mcp` launchers, so editor and agent integrations resolve the project-local binary instead of whatever happens to be on `PATH`. For one-off use, run `npx fallow` without installing. Other channels (cargo, Docker, prebuilt binaries) are covered in the [installation guide](https://fallow.tools/docs/installation/).

## Quick start

```bash
npx fallow                       # Full pipeline: dead code + duplication + health
npx fallow audit                 # Gate only what a PR changed: verdict pass/warn/fail
npx fallow health --score        # 0 to 100 health score with a letter grade
npx fallow dupes                 # Duplication; modes strict, mild (default), weak, semantic
npx fallow fix --dry-run         # Preview automatic cleanup
```

## Output and exit codes

Add `--format json --quiet` to any command for one typed JSON document on stdout. Exit code 1 means findings, not failure; 0 means no enforced gate failed (or an audit pass or warn verdict). Bare `fallow` in a machine format exits 0 on findings unless you pass `--fail-on-issues`; 2 is a validation or runtime error, reported as a JSON error envelope rather than a stack trace. License, coverage setup, network, and security-gate workflows use additional documented codes; read `fallow schema.exit_codes` instead of suppressing the process status.

Parsing the output in TypeScript? Import the typed shapes, version-pinned to the CLI you install:

```ts
import type { CheckOutput, FallowJsonOutput } from "fallow/types";
```

Every issue carries an `actions[]` array with an `auto_fixable` flag, so scripts and agents know which findings they can hand to `fallow fix`. The full contract lives at [fallow.tools/docs](https://fallow.tools/docs/).

## What fallow reports

- Unused files, exports, types, enum and class members, and dependencies
- Circular dependencies and re-export cycles
- Code duplication as clone families, across four detection modes
- Complexity hotspots and a 0 to 100 health score
- Architecture boundary violations, with zero-config presets
- Design-system styling drift for CSS and CSS-in-JS (Sass/Less, CSS Modules, Tailwind, styled-components, Emotion, and more)
- A changed-file PR gate with per-finding attribution (`fallow audit`)
- Optional TypeScript checker evidence for exact symbol use, affected files, targeted tests, cross-file private type leaks, and public-signature coupling (`--type-aware`)
- Optional production coverage with Fallow Cloud: hot paths, cold code, runtime-weighted health (licensed; a single local coverage capture is free)

### Optional TypeScript semantic evidence

Default analysis stays Rust-native and syntactic. Use `--type-aware` when a
cleanup or refactor needs exact checker-backed identity across aliases,
re-exports, packages, or tests:

```bash
npx fallow dead-code --unused-class-members --type-aware --format json --quiet
npx fallow fix --type-aware --dry-run --format json --quiet
npx fallow dead-code --type-aware --symbol-impact src/api.ts:Client --format json --quiet
npx fallow health --type-aware --type-coupling --format json --quiet
```

This complements `tsc --noEmit` and Oxlint. It does not emit compiler
diagnostics or duplicate local typed lint rules. If the optional companion
cannot prove a result safely, fallow retains the finding and reports why.
Required interface, abstract, and override members are removed from the
findings. A class member is automatically fixable only with complete
closed-world evidence and a matching declaration guard.

## Built for agents

Agents can query symbol importers, usage evidence, PR changes, and available cleanup actions.

The bundled `fallow-mcp` server lives in `node_modules/.bin/` when installed as a devDependency, so launch it through your package manager's runner:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fallow": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["--yes", "--package", "fallow", "fallow-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

`--package fallow` selects the npm package that provides the `fallow-mcp` launcher. For a project-local install, use `"command": "pnpm"` with `"args": ["exec", "fallow-mcp"]`, or `"command": "yarn"` with `"args": ["fallow-mcp"]`. A globally installed `fallow-mcp` works as `"command": "fallow-mcp"` directly. See the [MCP integration guide](https://fallow.tools/docs/integrations/mcp/).

For a verified project-local install, `npx fallow agent install` registers the MCP server with `npx --no fallow-mcp`. It also writes the skill, an `AGENTS.md` task map, and the commit/push gate for every harness it detects (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor); `--dry-run` shows the plan first.

The package also ships two version-matched agent skills: `skills/fallow` for analysis and `skills/fallow-setup` for setting up code-quality tooling. `fallow/capabilities.json` mirrors `fallow schema` for tools that need CLI and issue-surface metadata without spawning the binary. TanStack Intent discovers the skills and the metadata from `node_modules`:

```bash
npx @tanstack/intent list
npx @tanstack/intent load fallow#fallow
npx @tanstack/intent load fallow#fallow-setup
```

## Framework support

Over 100 built-in framework plugins covering Next.js, Nuxt, Remix, Qwik, SvelteKit, Gatsby, Astro, Angular, NestJS, AdonisJS, Ember, Expo Router, Vite, Webpack, Vitest, Jest, Playwright, Cypress, Storybook, ESLint, TypeScript, Tailwind, UnoCSS, Prisma, Drizzle, Convex, Turborepo, Hardhat, and more. Entry points are auto-detected from `package.json`, so the first run needs no configuration.

## Configuration

Fallow starts without a config file. To customize the analysis, let [`fallow recommend`](https://fallow.tools/docs/cli/recommend/) propose a config from the detected stack, run `fallow init`, or create a config file in your project root.

`fallow recommend` is read-only. With `--format json`, it returns the full decision set for agents. It points TypeScript projects to the optional `--type-aware` pass without enabling it.

To create a config manually, use a file like this in your project root:

```jsonc
// .fallowrc.json
{
  "$schema": "./node_modules/fallow/schema.json",
  "entry": ["src/workers/*.ts", "scripts/*.ts"],
  "ignorePatterns": ["**/*.generated.ts"],
  "rules": {
    "unused-files": "error",
    "unused-exports": "warn",
    "unused-types": "off"
  }
}
```

`$schema` gives editors autocomplete and validation and has no effect on analysis. The npm package ships a version-aligned schema at `./node_modules/fallow/schema.json`, so validation works offline with no editor trust prompt. TOML works too: `fallow init --toml` creates `fallow.toml`. Full reference: [configuration overview](https://fallow.tools/docs/configuration/overview/).

## Documentation

- [fallow.tools/docs](https://fallow.tools/docs/)
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow)
- [Plugin authoring guide](https://github.com/fallow-rs/fallow/blob/main/docs/plugin-authoring.md)

## License

MIT

entries.description:
Use this tool to create a structured task list for your current coding session. This helps you track progress, organize complex tasks, and demonstrate thoroughness to the user.
It also helps the user understand the progress of the task and overall progress of their requests.

## When to Use This Tool

Use this tool proactively in these scenarios:

- Complex multi-step tasks - When a task requires 3 or more distinct steps or actions
- Non-trivial and complex tasks - Tasks that require careful planning or multiple operations
- Plan mode - When using plan mode, create a task list to track the work
- User explicitly requests todo list - When the user directly asks you to use the todo list
- User provides multiple tasks - When users provide a list of things to be done (numbered or comma-separated)
- After receiving new instructions - Immediately capture user requirements as tasks
- When you start working on a task - Mark it as in_progress BEFORE beginning work
- After completing a task - Mark it as completed and add any new follow-up tasks discovered during implementation

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Skip using this tool when:
- There is only a single, straightforward task
- The task is trivial and tracking it provides no organizational benefit
- The task can be completed in less than 3 trivial steps
- The task is purely conversational or informational

NOTE that you should not use this tool if there is only one trivial task to do. In this case you are better off just doing the task directly.

## Task Fields

- **subject**: A brief, actionable title in imperative form (e.g., "Fix authentication bug in login flow")
- **description**: What needs to be done
- **activeForm** (optional): Present continuous form shown in the spinner when the task is in_progress (e.g., "Fixing authentication bug"). If omitted, the spinner shows the subject instead.

All tasks are created with status `pending`.

## Tips

- Create tasks with clear, specific subjects that describe the outcome
- After creating tasks, use TaskUpdate to set up dependencies (blocks/blockedBy) if needed
- Check TaskList first to avoid creating duplicate tasks

entries.name: TaskList
entries.description:
Use this tool to list all tasks in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

- To see what tasks are available to work on (status: 'pending', no owner, not blocked)
- To check overall progress on the project
- To find tasks that are blocked and need dependencies resolved
- After completing a task, to check for newly unblocked work or claim the next available task
- **Prefer working on tasks in ID order** (lowest ID first) when multiple tasks are available, as earlier tasks often set up context for later ones

## Output

Returns a summary of each task:
- **id**: Task identifier (use with TaskGet, TaskUpdate)
- **subject**: Brief description of the task
- **status**: 'pending', 'in_progress', or 'completed'
- **owner**: Agent ID if assigned, empty if available
- **blockedBy**: List of open task IDs that must be resolved first (tasks with blockedBy cannot be claimed until dependencies resolve)

Use TaskGet with a specific task ID to view full details including description and comments.

entries.name: TaskUpdate
entries.description:
Use this tool to update a task in the task list.

## When to Use This Tool

**Mark tasks as resolved:**
- When you have completed the work described in a task
- When a task is no longer needed or has been superseded
- IMPORTANT: Always mark your assigned tasks as resolved when you finish them
- After resolving, call TaskList to find your next task

- ONLY mark a task as completed when you have FULLY accomplished it
- If you encounter errors, blockers, or cannot finish, keep the task as in_progress
- When blocked, create a new task describing what needs to be resolved
- Never mark a task as completed if:
  - Tests are failing
  - Implementation is partial
  - You encountered unresolved errors
  - You couldn't find necessary files or dependencies

**Delete tasks:**
- When a task is no longer relevant or was created in error
- Setting status to `deleted` permanently removes the task

**Update task details:**
- When requirements change or become clearer
- When establishing dependencies between tasks

## Fields You Can Update

- **status**: The task status (see Status Workflow below)
- **subject**: Change the task title (imperative form, e.g., "Run tests")
- **description**: Change the task description
- **activeForm**: Present continuous form shown in spinner when in_progress (e.g., "Running tests")
- **owner**: Change the task owner (agent name)
- **metadata**: Merge metadata keys into the task (set a key to null to delete it)
- **addBlocks**: Mark tasks that cannot start until this one completes
- **addBlockedBy**: Mark tasks that must complete before this one can start

## Status Workflow

Status progresses: `pending` → `in_progress` → `completed`

Use `deleted` to permanently remove a task.

## Staleness

Make sure to read a task's latest state using `TaskGet` before updating it.

## Examples

Mark task as in progress when starting work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "in_progress"}
```

Mark task as completed after finishing work:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "completed"}
```

Delete a task:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "status": "deleted"}
```

Claim a task by setting owner:
```json
{"taskId": "1", "owner": "my-name"}
```

Set up task dependencies:
```json
{"taskId": "2", "addBlockedBy": ["1"]}
```

--- name: react-start description: >- React bindings for TanStack Start: createStart, StartClient, StartServer, React-specific imports, re-exports from @tanstack/react-router, full project setup with React, useServerFn hook. metadata: type: framework library: tanstack-start library_version: '1.168.32' framework: react requires: - start-core sources: - TanStack/router:packages/react-start/src - TanStack/router:docs/start/framework/react/build-from-scratch.md --- # React Start (`@tanstack/react-start`) This is the React Start entry skill. Use the workflow below, then load only the package skill that owns the boundary you are changing. Do not read `start-core`, Router Core, and React Router manuals in full before starting. For React Server Components patterns, see [react-start/server-components](./server-components/SKILL.md). > **CRITICAL**: All code is ISOMORPHIC by default. Loaders run on BOTH server and client. Use `createServerFn` for server-only logic. > **CRITICAL**: Do not confuse `@tanstack/react-start` with Next.js or Remix. They are completely different frameworks with different APIs. > **CRITICAL**: Types are FULLY INFERRED. Never cast, never annotate inferred values. ## Full-Stack Workflow 1. Define the route and component with `createFileRoute`. 2. Put private or server-only reads and writes in `createServerFn`; call reads directly from loaders. 3. Use `useServerFn` for component mutations, then invalidate the router or query cache after the write resolves. 4. Enforce auth in every private server function or server route. Add `beforeLoad` separately for navigation UX. 5. Run the initial SSR path, client navigation, mutation plus reload, direct anonymous endpoint request, runtime response assertion, type tests, and production build. Load `start-core/server-routes` instead of `server-functions` only when a raw HTTP endpoint is required. Load `router-core/*` only for the specific routing concern involved, such as params or search validation. ## Package API Surface `@tanstack/react-start` re-exports everything from `@tanstack/start-client-core` plus: - `useServerFn` — React hook for calling server functions from components All core APIs (`createServerFn`, `createMiddleware`, `createStart`, `createIsomorphicFn`, `createServerOnlyFn`, `createClientOnlyFn`) are available from `@tanstack/react-start`. Server utilities (`getRequest`, `getRequestHeader`, `setResponseHeader`, `setResponseHeaders`, `setResponseStatus`) are imported from `@tanstack/react-start/server`. ## Full Project Setup ### 1. Install Dependencies ```bash npm i @tanstack/react-start @tanstack/react-router react react-dom npm i -D vite @vitejs/plugin-react typescript @types/react @types/react-dom ``` ### 2. package.json ```json { "type": "module", "scripts": { "dev": "vite dev", "build": "vite build", "start": "node .output/server/index.mjs" } } ``` ### 3. tsconfig.json ```json { "compilerOptions": { "jsx": "react-jsx", "moduleResolution": "Bundler", "module": "ESNext", "target": "ES2022", "skipLibCheck": true, "strictNullChecks": true } } ``` ### 4. vite.config.ts ```ts import { defineConfig } from 'vite' import { tanstackStart } from '@tanstack/react-start/plugin/vite' import viteReact from '@vitejs/plugin-react' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [ tanstackStart(), // MUST come before react() viteReact(), ], }) ``` ### 5. Router Factory (src/router.tsx) ```tsx import { createRouter } from '@tanstack/react-router' import { routeTree } from './routeTree.gen' export function getRouter() { const router = createRouter({ routeTree, scrollRestoration: true, }) return router } ``` ### 6. Root Route (src/routes/\_\_root.tsx) ```tsx import type { ReactNode } from 'react' import { Outlet, createRootRoute, HeadContent, Scripts, } from '@tanstack/react-router' export const Route = createRootRoute({ head: () => ({ meta: [ { charSet: 'utf-8' }, { name: 'viewport', content: 'width=device-width, initial-scale=1' }, { title: 'My TanStack Start App' }, ], }), component: RootComponent, }) function RootComponent() { return ( ) } function RootDocument({ children }: Readonly<{ children: ReactNode }>) { return ( {children} ) } ``` ### 7. Index Route (src/routes/index.tsx) ```tsx import { createFileRoute } from '@tanstack/react-router' import { createServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start' const getGreeting = createServerFn({ method: 'GET' }).handler(async () => { return 'Hello from TanStack Start!' }) export const Route = createFileRoute('/')({ loader: () => getGreeting(), component: HomePage, }) function HomePage() { const greeting = Route.useLoaderData() return

{greeting}

} ``` ## useServerFn Hook Use `useServerFn` to call server functions from React components with proper integration: ```tsx import { createServerFn, useServerFn } from '@tanstack/react-start' const updatePost = createServerFn({ method: 'POST' }) .validator((data: { id: string; title: string }) => data) .handler(async ({ data }) => { await db.posts.update(data.id, { title: data.title }) return { success: true } }) function EditPostForm({ postId }: { postId: string }) { const updatePostFn = useServerFn(updatePost) const [title, setTitle] = useState('') return (
{ e.preventDefault() await updatePostFn({ data: { id: postId, title } }) }} > setTitle(e.target.value)} />
) } ``` ## Global Start Configuration (src/start.ts) ```tsx import { createStart, createMiddleware } from '@tanstack/react-start' const requestLogger = createMiddleware().server(async ({ next, request }) => { console.log(`${request.method} ${request.url}`) return next() }) export const startInstance = createStart(() => ({ requestMiddleware: [requestLogger], })) ``` ## React-Specific Components All routing components from `@tanstack/react-router` work in Start: - `` — not needed in Start (handled automatically) - `` — renders matched child route - `` — type-safe navigation - `` — declarative redirect - `` — renders head tags (must be in ``) - `` — renders body scripts (must be in ``) - `` — renders deferred data with Suspense - `` — renders children only after hydration - `` — error boundary ## Hooks Reference All hooks from `@tanstack/react-router` work in Start: - `useRouter()` — router instance @tanstack/react-start/skills/: lifecycle react-start @tanstack/react-start/skills/react-start: SKILL.md server-components

+/**
+ * The block vocabulary the planner composes from (HOME-7). The server returns an
+ * ordered list; the client maps `type` to a component and `placement` to a generic slot.
+ */
+import { z } from "zod";
+import { BlockType, zModeKind, zPlacement, zProvenance, zSection } from "./enums.ts";
+import { zIsoDateTime, zLocalDate, zNotifyAction } from "./message.ts";
+
+const base = {
+  /** Stable across re-plans of the same day, so dismissals stick (HOME-4). */
+  id: z.string(),
+  section: zSection,
+  placement: zPlacement,
+  /** One line you could check yourself (HOME-3). */
+  reason: z.string(),
+  provenance: zProvenance,
+};
+
+export const zContextBlock = z.object({
+  ...base,
+  type: z.literal(BlockType.context),
+  title: z.string(),
+  line: z.string(),
+});
+
+export const zModeBlock = z.object({
+  ...base,
+  type: z.literal(BlockType.mode),
+  mode: zModeKind,
+  heading: z.string(),
+  /** The one suggested thing; null when there is nothing worth doing. */
+  pick: z
+    .object({
+      ref: z.string(),
+      title: z.string(),
+      why: z.string(),
+      actions: z.array(zNotifyAction),
+    })
+    .nullable(),
+  /** Fixed things still happening anyway (MOM-5). */
+  stillHappening: z.array(z.object({ id: z.string(), text: z.string(), provenance: zProvenance })),
+});
+
+export const zEventBlock = z.object({
+  ...base,
+  type: z.literal(BlockType.event),
+  time: z.string().nullable(),
+  title: z.string(),
+  detail: z.string(),
+  ref: z.string(),
+});
+
+export const zSuggestionBlock = z.object({
+  ...base,
+  type: z.literal(BlockType.suggestion),
+  title: z.string(),
+  ref: z.string(),
+  actions: z.array(zNotifyAction),
+});
+
+export const zAlertBlock = z.object({
+  ...base,
+  type: z.literal(BlockType.alert),
+  title: z.string(),
+  ref: z.string(),
+  /** At most one action (Components canvas: "one action"). */
+  action: zNotifyAction.nullable(),
+});
+
+export const zArrivalBlock = z.object({
+  ...base,
+  type: z.literal(BlockType.arrival),
+  shop: z.string(),
+  when: z.string(),
+  ref: z.string(),
+});
+
+export const zBacklogPickBlock = z.object({
+  ...base,
+  type: z.literal(BlockType.backlogPick),
+  title: z.string(),
+  ref: z.string(),
+  actions: z.array(zNotifyAction),
+});
+
+export const zComposerBlock = z.object({
+  ...base,
+  type: z.literal(BlockType.composer),
+  placeholder: z.string(),
+});
+
+export const zBlock = z.discriminatedUnion("type", [
+  zContextBlock,
+  zModeBlock,
+  zEventBlock,
+  zSuggestionBlock,
+  zAlertBlock,
+  zArrivalBlock,
+  zBacklogPickBlock,
+  zComposerBlock,
+]);
+export type Block = z.infer<typeof zBlock>;
+export type ContextBlock = z.infer<typeof zContextBlock>;
+export type ModeBlock = z.infer<typeof zModeBlock>;
+export type EventBlock = z.infer<typeof zEventBlock>;
+export type SuggestionBlock = z.infer<typeof zSuggestionBlock>;
+export type AlertBlock = z.infer<typeof zAlertBlock>;
+export type ArrivalBlock = z.infer<typeof zArrivalBlock>;
+export type BacklogPickBlock = z.infer<typeof zBacklogPickBlock>;
+export type ComposerBlock = z.infer<typeof zComposerBlock>;
+
+/** PLT-4: a day's plan is one row of ordered blocks; every version is kept. */
+export const zPlan = z.object({
+  date: zLocalDate,
+  version: z.number().int(),
+  createdAt: zIsoDateTime,
+  blocks: z.array(zBlock),
+});
+export type Plan = z.infer<typeof zPlan>;
+
+/** What the screen reads: the latest plan with responses already applied. */
+export const zScreen = z.object({
+  date: zLocalDate,
+  version: z.number().int(),
+  generatedAt: zIsoDateTime,
+  blocks: z.array(zBlock),
+});
+export type Screen = z.infer<typeof zScreen>;

+/**
+ * Records each domain exposes through its tRPC router (CODE-5). Routers take their
+ * input and output types from here; the UI reads the same shapes.
+ */
+import { z } from "zod";
+import {
+  zActionKind,
+  zBacklogStatus,
+  zBacklogTag,
+  zChannel,
+  zDayPart,
+  zDeliveryChannel,
+  zJobStatus,
+  zLearningEventKind,
+  zModeKind,
+  zModelProvider,
+  zNurseryEventKind,
+  zPersonRole,
+  zQuestionTopic,
+  zRuleKind,
+  zShoppingStatus,
+  zTimerKind,
+  zUrgency,
+  zWeekday,
+  zWellbeingFactor,
+} from "./enums.ts";
+import { zIsoDateTime, zLocalDate } from "./message.ts";
+
+// ── household ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+/** PRV-4: a child is a first name and nursery days, nothing else. */
+export const zPerson = z.object({
+  id: z.string(),
+  name: z.string(),
+  role: zPersonRole,
+  nurseryDays: z.array(zWeekday),
+});
+export type Person = z.infer<typeof zPerson>;
+
+export const zSitter = z.object({ id: z.string(), name: z.string(), knownFreeDays: z.array(zWeekday) });
+export type Sitter = z.infer<typeof zSitter>;
+
+export const zRouting = z.record(zUrgency, zDeliveryChannel);
+export type Routing = z.infer<typeof zRouting>;
+
+export const zPersonSettings = z.object({
+  person: z.string(),
+  dailyMessageBudget: z.number().int().min(0),
+  quietStartHour: z.number().int().min(0).max(23),
+  quietEndHour: z.number().int().min(0).max(23),
+  routing: zRouting,
+  wellbeingEnabled: z.boolean(),
+  healthInScore: z.boolean(),
+});
+export type PersonSettings = z.infer<typeof zPersonSettings>;
+
+export const zHouseholdSettings = z.object({
+  household: z.string(),
+  name: z.string(),
+  timezone: z.string(),
+  retainMessages: z.boolean(),
+  latitude: z.number(),
+  longitude: z.number(),
+});
+export type HouseholdSettings = z.infer<typeof zHouseholdSettings>;
+
+export const zMode = z.object({
+  id: z.string(),
+  mode: zModeKind,
+  setBy: z.string(),
+  setAt: zIsoDateTime,
+  /** MOM-4: ends at midnight unless extended. */
+  endsAt: zIsoDateTime,
+});
+export type Mode = z.infer<typeof zMode>;
+
+export const zBinsRule = z.object({
+  kind: z.literal("bins"),
+  collectionDay: zWeekday,
+  /** Bins alternate by ISO week parity: `even` weeks and `odd` weeks. */
+  evenWeeks: z.array(z.string()),
+  oddWeeks: z.array(z.string()),
+});
+export const zChoreRule = z.object({
+  kind: z.literal("chore"),
+  title: z.string(),
+  everyDays: z.number().int().min(1),
+  anchorDate: zLocalDate,
+});
+export const zRuleSpec = z.discriminatedUnion("kind", [zBinsRule, zChoreRule]);
+export type RuleSpec = z.infer<typeof zRuleSpec>;
+
+export const zRule = z.object({
+  id: z.string(),
+  kind: zRuleKind,
+  spec: zRuleSpec,
+  createdBy: z.string(),
+  createdAt: zIsoDateTime,
+});
+export type Rule = z.infer<typeof zRule>;
+
+export const zNurseryTerm = z.object({ id: z.string(), start: zLocalDate, end: zLocalDate });
+export type NurseryTerm = z.infer<typeof zNurseryTerm>;
+
+export const zNurseryEvent = z.object({
+  id: z.string(),
+  kind: zNurseryEventKind,
+  date: zLocalDate,
+  title: z.string(),
+  /** Who is covering childcare that day, if anyone. */
+  coveredBy: z.string().nullable(),
+});
+export type NurseryEvent = z.infer<typeof zNurseryEvent>;
+
+export const zSitterBooking = z.object({ id: z.string(), sitter: z.string(), date: zLocalDate, recordedBy: z.string() });
+export type SitterBooking = z.infer<typeof zSitterBooking>;
+
+export const zWellbeingIdea = z.object({ id: z.string(), text: z.string(), createdBy: z.string() });
+export type WellbeingIdea = z.infer<typeof zWellbeingIdea>;
+
+// ── calendar ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+export const zCalendarEvent = z.object({
+  id: z.string(),
+  externalId: z.string(),
+  title: z.string(),
+  start: zIsoDateTime,
+  end: zIsoDateTime,
+  allDay: z.boolean(),
+  /** Household people attending. */
+  attendees: z.array(z.string()),
+  /** People this event takes out of the house. */
+  away: z.array(z.string()),
+  /** Work commitment (for WB-1). */
+  work: z.boolean(),
+  /** Someone has the kids alone during this event (for WB-1). */
+  soloWithKids: z.string().nullable(),
+});
+export type CalendarEvent = z.infer<typeof zCalendarEvent>;
+
+// ── backlog ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+
+export const zBacklogItem = z.object({
+  id: z.string(),
+  text: z.string(),
+  tags: z.array(zBacklogTag),
+  /** Tags a person confirmed or corrected; the rest are the app's guesses (CAP-3). */
+  confirmedTags: z.boolean(),
+  status: zBacklogStatus,
+  notNowCount: z.number().int(),
+  createdBy: z.string(),
+  createdVia: zChannel,
+  createdAt: zIsoDateTime,
+});
+export type BacklogItem = z.infer<typeof zBacklogItem>;
+
+export const zBacklogView = z.object({
+  soon: z.array(z.object({ item: zBacklogItem, slot: z.string() })),
+  waiting: z.array(z.object({ item: zBacklogItem, waitingFor: z.string() })),
+  justAdded: z.array(zBacklogItem),
+  parked: z.array(zBacklogItem),
+});
+export type BacklogView = z.infer<typeof zBacklogView>;
+

content.content:
# CI gate

Add one gate to the CI provider that the project already uses. Exit code 0 means that the gate passed. Exit code 1 means that the gate found error-severity findings or that the audit result is `fail`. Exit code 2 means invalid input or an execution error. Do not force a successful exit status, because that hides the gate result.

## Select the gate

| Gate | Command | Fails on | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| Changed-code gate | `fallow audit` | Findings that the change introduces in the changed files | Not necessary |
| Whole-project gate | `fallow` | Every error-severity finding in the project | Necessary when the first run has many findings |

Start with the changed-code gate. `fallow audit` uses `--gate new-only` by default, so findings that existed before the change do not fail it. The audit needs the git history of the base ref. In CI, fetch the full history.

## GitHub Actions

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
  with:
    fetch-depth: 0
- uses: fallow-rs/fallow@v3
  with:
    command: audit
```

The Action installs the Fallow version that `package.json` names. To start in report-only mode, add `fail-on-issues: false`. Remove it when the team accepts the gate.

## GitLab CI

```yaml
include:
  - remote: 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fallow-rs/fallow/v<version>/ci/gitlab-ci.yml'

fallow:
  extends: .fallow
  variables:
    FALLOW_COMMAND: "audit"
```

Replace `<version>` with the installed Fallow version. When the runners cannot reach `raw.githubusercontent.com`, run `fallow ci-template gitlab --vendor` and include the vendored files locally.

## Other CI providers

Run the CLI directly after the dependencies are installed:

```bash
npx fallow audit --base origin/main --format json --quiet
```

Use the runner of the detected package manager, for example `pnpm exec fallow`.

## Baselines

A whole-project gate on an existing project often reports a large backlog on the first run. Save a baseline of that backlog, so that the gate fails only on new findings:

```bash
fallow dead-code --format json --quiet --save-baseline fallow-baselines/dead-code.json
fallow health --format json --quiet --save-baseline fallow-baselines/health.json
fallow dupes --format json --quiet --save-baseline fallow-baselines/dupes.json
```

Commit the baseline files. Pass each file to the matching command with `--baseline <path>`. On bare `fallow`, `--baseline` holds the dead-code baseline only: pass the health and duplication files with `--health-baseline` and `--dupes-baseline`. The GitHub Action takes them as the `baseline`, `health-baseline` and `dupes-baseline` inputs, and the GitLab template as `FALLOW_BASELINE`, `FALLOW_HEALTH_BASELINE` and `FALLOW_DUPES_BASELINE`. `fallow audit` uses `--dead-code-baseline`, `--health-baseline`, and `--dupes-baseline` instead. `--fail-on-baseline-growth` makes a committed baseline shrink-only. After a fix, `fallow baselines prune` removes the entries that match no current finding, so `--fail-on-stale-baseline` stays green. Point `audit.deadCodeBaseline`, `audit.healthBaseline` and `audit.dupesBaseline` at the files so that one command prunes all three. Tell the user how many findings the baseline contains, and suggest that the team removes them by category.

You are the fork building the WEB APP + DESIGN SYSTEM. Work only under `web/` and `design/` (plus adding web deps to root package.json via pnpm and a `web` entry in tsconfig include if needed). Do not touch server/, contracts/ (except: you MAY add purely presentational as-const label maps to contracts/src/enums.ts if a label is missing — avoid if possible), practice/, tools/.

Goal: a TanStack Start PWA in SPA mode (`tanstackStart({ spa: { enabled: true } })`, vite root `web/`, config `web/vite.config.ts`, output `web/dist/client` with the shell as `_shell.html` or `index.html` — the server's static handler in server/http/app.ts serves `web/dist/client/_shell.html` else `index.html`, and files by path). Dev server on port 3000 proxying `/api` and `/mcp` to http://localhost:3001 with HMR.

1. DESIGN SYSTEM in `web/src/design-system/`: tokens from design/README.md + the canvas files (design/canvas/*.dc.html) as CSS custom properties (`tokens.css`) AND a single source `design/tokens.json` (shared token set for Paper, QA-3) — add a vitest test that tokens.css and tokens.json agree. Components rebuilt faithfully from the canvas markup (Manrope via Google Fonts link is fine; fall back to system-ui): Screen/Page shell, Header (title + context line + secondary nav links), SectionLabel, Card, EventRow, SuggestionCard (green, Doing it / Not today), AlertCard (amber, one action), ArrivalRow, BacklogPickCard (Pencil it in / Not now), ModeCard ("If you do one thing" + Done / Cal can do it→"<other adult> can do it" / Not today + still-happening list), Composer (text input + mic button; mic uses Web Speech API when available and sends `spoken: true`), Button (primary/secondary/ghost/alert variants, min 44px tap target ALWAYS — HOME-10; the backlog tag chips drawn at 32px in the canvas must still have a ≥44px hit area), Chip (tag chip, tap to toggle), List, Reply bubble (one-line answer from the house), Field/Toggle/Stepper for settings. Colour means provenance: green = planner suggestion, amber = rule-derived alert, grey = calendar/email fact. No tab bar, no red badges (HOME-9). Screens may ONLY use design-system components: add a vitest test (`web/src/design-system/usage.test.ts`) that fails if any file under web/src/routes or web/src/screens contains `style=`, a raw hex colour, or imports a CSS file other than via the design system.

2. SERVER-DRIVEN HOME (HOME-7): `web/src/blocks/BlockRenderer.tsx` maps `block.type` (contracts BlockType) to a component with an exhaustive switch; blocks come ordered from the server; group consecutive blocks by `section` (heading = contracts SectionLabel[section], empty label = no heading) and put each run into a generic slot by `placement` (header/main/aside/focus/footer). Wide screens: main + aside two columns (like design/canvas/Main.dc.html); `focus` placement = centered single column (SlowDay.dc.html); phone (<700px): everything one column, nothing cut off (Phone.dc.html). The client owns NO screen-specific layout logic. The composer block always renders (footer).

3. DATA: use `@trpc/client` + `@tanstack/react-query` + `@trpc/tanstack-react-query` against `/api/trpc` typed with `import type { ViewsRouter } from "../../server/views/router.ts"` (type-only import). Procedures: me, screen({date?}), week, backlog, shop, settings, conversation, run({id}), trace({id}), runLog, spend; mutations setTags, bringBack, removeBacklog, updateMySettings, updateHousehold, editRhythm, forgetSentence, addWellbeingIdea, removeWellbeingIdea, addHealthEntry. Saying anything / tapping any action button = `POST /api/messages` with body `AppMessageInput` from contracts/src/views.ts (`{text, ref?, action?, value?, spoken?, clientId}`; clientId = crypto.randomUUID() per user action, reused on retry). For a button: text = the button label, ref = action.ref, action = action.kind, value = action.value. Optimistic update: hide a dismissed/done block immediately (HOME-5), then refetch. Live: `EventSource('/api/live')` events `change` with `{topic}` → invalidate all queries (simple) — reconnect automatically. Tapping a block's title (not a button) selects it as context: the composer shows a small "About: <title>" chip and the next message carries `ref` (MOM-7). Show the latest reply from `conversation` under the composer for ~1 minute after sending (MOM-2: one line answer). Login page `/login` posting `/api/login` `{username,password}` then navigating to `next`.

4. ROUTES: `/` home (screen), `/backlog` (three groups Could go soon / Waiting for the right moment / Just added with tag chips — tapping a chip toggles that tag via setTags; parked count + Show parked with Bring back; dump box composer posts a message), `/week`, `/shop` (basket, recent shopping requests with status/chosen product, questions with 2–3 option buttons → POST message with ref `shopping:<id>`, action `answer`, value sku; lists app lists), `/settings` (my message budget + quiet hours steppers, routing table per urgency, retention toggle (household), wellbeing on/off + score breakdown table, health tracking entry only if me.healthOwner, learned sentences each with a delete button and an editable "about every N days" for rhythms, the wellbeing ideas list editable, rules list read-only), `/runs` (run log: jobs + timer runs with missed ones flagged), `/runs/$id` (shopping run log + screenshots), `/trace/$id` (job trace), `/spend` (monthly AI spend). Home nav links: Backlog, Shop, Week (+ Settings in a quiet spot) — secondary, out of the way.

5. PWA (HOME-6): web manifest (display: standalone, plus `display_override: ["fullscreen","standalone"]`), icons (generate simple PNG icons programmatically or SVG), apple-mobile-web-app-capable meta + apple-touch-icon, theme colour from tokens; a service worker that caches the app shell and the last successful `screen` response so it still renders offline; the home screen re-fetches when the local date changes (check every minute and on visibilitychange) and when SSE reconnects, so after being left open all week it shows today's plan.

6. Verify: `npx tsc -p .` and `npx oxlint --type-aware` clean for your files (follow the repo lint rules: named exports only except where the framework requires default exports — add those files to the oxlint override list in .oxlintrc.json; sorted import members; no `any`, no `!`), `pnpm exec vitest run web` passes, `pnpm exec vite build --config web/vite.config.ts` (or whatever build command you set up; add a root script `"build:web"`) succeeds. Then render the built app with Playwright (preinstalled; `require('playwright')`, chromium.launch()) against a tiny throwaway fixture server in your scratchpad that serves the build and fakes `/api/trpc` responses with realistic block data mirroring design/canvas/Main.dc.html, SlowDay.dc.html, Phone.dc.html, Backlog.dc.html — take screenshots at 1180×820 and 390×844 and compare them visually against the canvas (open the canvas files in Playwright too, removing the support.js script tag). Iterate until they match closely. Save final screenshots into the scratchpad directory and list their absolute paths in your report.

You are the fork building the AUTOMATIONS helper (AUT-2, AUT-3, AUT-4, AUT-6, AUT-7) and the PRACTICE SUPERMARKET (QA-9). Work only under `helper/`, `practice/supermarket/`, and a new client file `server/integrations/shopping-helper.ts` (+ its test). Do not edit other existing files except adding deps with pnpm and adding entries to tsconfig include / vitest include if needed.

1. `practice/supermarket/`: a realistic small online-supermarket web app (hono + @hono/node-server, server-rendered HTML) using `practice/data.ts` `supermarket` catalogue: /login (username+password form, session cookie; accounts in memory: the practice account `practice-shopper` / password read from env or default), /search?q= (results list, product cards with name/price/"Add" button), /product/:sku, /basket (items with quantity and remove buttons, delivery date, "Change delivery slot" link to /slots, "Checkout" button to /checkout), /slots, /checkout (would place the order). In-memory state; export `startSupermarket({port})` returning {url, close, state} and a CLI entry. Expose `GET /practice-api/basket` JSON for tests. Port default 3002.

2. `helper/`: the sealed helper SERVICE — its own process (own container later): hono HTTP API on port 3003, every request must carry `Authorization: Bearer ${HELPER_TOKEN}`. It reads the supermarket credentials from a locked store: a file path in `SUPERMARKET_CREDENTIALS_FILE` (JSON {url, username, password}); refuse to start if the file is group/world readable (mode & 0o077) — that is the locked store; NEVER log or return the password: wrap all log lines through a redactor that replaces the password and username with *** and add a test proving log lines and API responses never contain them (AUT-2). Endpoints: POST /tasks/shopping/add-item {item}, POST /tasks/shopping/add-product {sku}, GET /tasks/shopping/basket. Implement, each in its own file with a vitest test that uses a local fake HTTP server or injected fetch (no real network — the sandbox blocks most hosts):
1. `weather-open-meteo.ts`: `OpenMeteoWeather implements WeatherSource` — GET https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude&longitude&hourly=precipitation_probability,temperature_2m&timezone=<tz>&start_date=<date>&end_date=<date>; map to HourlyForecast (hour as local "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00"). Base URL injectable.
2. `google-calendar.ts`: `GoogleCalendarSource implements CalendarSource` — read-only (scope calendar.readonly; there must be NO method that writes — PRV-1; add a test asserting the class has no insert/patch/update/delete/move methods and that every HTTP call it makes is a GET). events.list with singleEvents=true and syncToken incremental sync (first sync: timeMin = now-1d, timeMax = now+60d; handle 410 Gone by full resync). Access token from a callback `getAccessToken(): Promise<string>`; also provide `refreshingTokenProvider({clientId, clientSecret, refreshToken, tokenUrl})` using the OAuth refresh_token grant. Map Google events → ExternalEvent: attendees mapped from attendee emails to person ids via an injected `personForEmail(email)`; organizer counts; `away` = attendees when the event has a location or is not tagged `#home` in the description; `work` = description/summary contains #work or event is from a work calendar id list; `soloWithKids` from description tag `#solo:<person>`; all-day events → start/end at local midnight. Cancelled events → deletedExternalIds. Document these conventions in a comment block (they are assumptions the household can change).

3. `telegram.ts`: `TelegramTransport implements MessengerTransport` — sendMessage(chat_id=address, text, reply_markup inline_keyboard from buttons, one row, callback_data ≤ 64 bytes — validate and throw if longer). Base URL `${TELEGRAM_API_BASE}/bot${token}`; never log the token (test it). Plus `parseTelegramUpdate(update)` → `{kind:'message', chatId, fromId, text, updateId, voiceFileId?} | {kind:'callback', chatId, fromId, data, updateId, callbackQueryId} | null` and `answerCallbackQuery`. Also `downloadVoice(fileId)` via getFile.
4. `s3-object-store.ts`: `S3ObjectStore implements ObjectStore` using @aws-sdk/client-s3 (installed) with forcePathStyle (MinIO), and CLIENT-SIDE encryption: AES-256-GCM with a 32-byte key (hex) — body stored as [12-byte IV][ciphertext][16-byte tag], plus request ServerSideEncryption: "AES256" header when `sse: true`. Test the encryption roundtrip with a fake S3 HTTP server (or by injecting a fake S3 client send) and prove stored bytes don't contain the plaintext (PLT-7). Also `FsObjectStore` (same encryption, files under a dir) for single-box dev.
5. `hindsight-memory.ts`: `HindsightMemory implements EpisodicMemory` using @vectorize-io/hindsight-client (inspect its API in node_modules) — one memory bank per (household, person): bank id `household-<household>-person-<person>`; retain → retain/put memory; recall → recall/search returning strings; forget → delete bank. Recall must never cross scopes (PLT-6) — test with a fake Hindsight HTTP server that the request path/bank id contains only that person's scope.
6. `transcriber.ts`: `AiSdkTranscriber implements Transcriber` using the Vercel AI SDK transcription API (`experimental_transcribe` or `transcribe` from "ai" — check what ai@7 exports) with a model passed in (provider is configuration; CODE-12 — do NOT import provider SDKs here, take a TranscriptionModel as constructor arg).
7. `index.ts`: `realPorts(env, clock)` building Ports from env (server/env.ts) where configured, returning which ports fell back to practice fakes (from practice/fakes.ts) when credentials are missing — return `{ ports, missing: string[] }`. Lists app (CAP-6): we do not know which lists app the household uses; keep the practice fake and list "lists" as missing with a comment.

Follow repo rules: strict TS with erasableSyntaxOnly (no parameter properties, no enums), named exports, sorted import members, no `any`, no non-null `!`, oxlint --type-aware clean. IMPORTANT lint rule CODE-13: any object key named timeout/maxRetries/etc. or `AbortSignal.timeout(...)` needs `Limits.<name>.value` + `// limit: <name>` — simply do not add timeouts/retries (none are needed). Name tests with verification IDs in brackets where relevant (e.g. `[PRV-1] google calendar source can only read`, `[PLT-7] objects are encrypted before they leave the process`, `[PLT-6] recall never crosses people`). Run `npx tsc -p .`, `npx oxlint --type-aware`, `pnpm exec vitest run server/integrations` until green.

- `http.ts`: the injectable fetch helper and error type.
- `fake-http.ts`: a local server that records requests, used by the tests.
- `weather-open-meteo.ts`: `OpenMeteoWeather`.
- `google-calendar.ts`: `GoogleCalendarSource`, which only ever sends GET requests and uses sync tokens, starting a full sync again on a 410. Also `refreshingTokenProvider`, `createWatchChannel` and `parseCalendarNotification`.
- `telegram.ts`: `TelegramTransport` with `send` (one-row inline keyboard, button data checked against the 64-byte limit), `answerCallbackQuery` and `downloadVoice`, plus `parseTelegramUpdate`.
- `s3-object-store.ts`: `S3ObjectStore` (path-style for MinIO, optional server-side encryption) and `FsObjectStore`. Both encrypt with AES-256-GCM, stored as IV, then ciphertext, then tag.
- `hindsight-memory.ts`: `HindsightMemory`, one bank per person per house (`household-<h>-person-<p>`); forgetting a person deletes their bank.
- `transcriber.ts`: `AiSdkTranscriber`, which uses `transcribe` from `ai` with the model passed in.
- `index.ts`: `realPorts(env, clock, { timeZone, personForEmail, shopping?, transcriptionModel?, workCalendarIds? })` returns `{ ports, missing }`.

**Tests, by verification ID**
- **PRV-1:** google calendar source can only read.
- **HOME-1, CH-6:** first sync covers yesterday to two months ahead, then syncs by token.
- **CH-6:** subscribes to change notifications with a shared token.
- **CH-4, PRV-6:** push-notification headers are parsed so the webhook can dedupe and check the token.
- **PLT-7:** objects are encrypted before they leave the process; tampered ciphertext is rejected; the disk store uses the same encryption and stays inside its folder.
- **PLT-6:** recall never crosses people or houses.
- **PRV-7:** forgetting a person deletes their bank.
- **CH-8:** buttons go out as an inline keyboard, and a tap comes back as a callback.
- **AUT-2:** the bot token never appears in an error or a log line.
- **MOM-8:** voice notes download through getFile and are transcribed through the AI SDK (also tagged CODE-12).
- **CH-1:** a text update becomes chat, sender, text and update id.
- **QA-9:** with nothing configured, every credentialed port falls back to the practice household and says so.
- **HOME-2, PRO-4:** the hourly forecast is read for one local day.
- The rest are untagged edge cases: 410 resync, token refresh caching, the 64-byte button limit, ignored updates, bad-key rejection.

**Assumptions and gaps you'll need to account for**
- **Calendar conventions:** `#home`, `#work`, `#solo:<person>`, organizer counts as attending, declined attendees are dropped, and all-day events run from local midnight. They're documented at the top of `google-calendar.ts` for the household to change.
- **Deletions after a 410:** a full resync only returns events that still exist, so anything deleted during the gap isn't reported.
- **Google credentials:** env has no client id or secret variables, so `GOOGLE_ACCESS_TOKEN_FILE` is read as a vault JSON file holding either `{client_id, client_secret, refresh_token}` or `{access_token}`.
- **Shopping helper and transcriber:** these are injected rather than built from env. `realPorts` falls back to the practice fakes and lists them as missing. I did not create `shopping-helper.ts`.
- **Lists app:** no real adapter, since we don't know which app the household uses; it's always reported missing (CAP-6).
- **Object storage default:** with no S3 configured, practice mode uses the in-memory store and real mode uses the encrypted disk store.
- **Retries:** the Hindsight client retries recall internally by default (on 429 or 503). I set no `maxAttempts`, so there is no limit configured anywhere for the CODE-13 lint rule to catch.</result>
